source.title: Implicit Regularization of Discrete Gradient Dynamics in Deep Linear Neural Networks
source.authors: G. Gidel; F. Bach; Simon Lacoste-Julien

record.file_problem: Full paper text supplied, including appendices; no apparent cutoff affecting the reported results.
record.tranche_reason: The paper tests whether gradient dynamics in an overparameterized model can produce implicitly regularized solutions with better generalization, using a two-layer linear network and reconstruction error rather than the claim versions’ natural-label test error setup.
record.gate_note: The paper reports a synthetic linear autoencoder comparison of linear and two-layer linear training dynamics, including reconstruction errors. It does not test fitting random labels, natural-label classification generalization, width sweeps, convolutional versus fully connected networks, adaptive optimizers, batch size, dropout, sharpness measures, or removal of memorized examples. Its classification-dataset table measures assumptions, not generalization outcomes.
record.test_reason: The study analyzes implicit regularization and synthetic matrix reconstruction in linear networks. Its results do not test any of V1–V8: reconstruction dynamics are a different outcome, and no width, optimizer, batch, dropout, sharpness, architecture-locality, or memorized-example comparison measures the named effects.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is substantially accurate. The authors prove sequential implicit rank regularization under specific assumptions and describe improved synthetic matrix reconstruction relative to the linear model. They suggest potential generalization benefits while explicitly limiting conclusions about standard deep networks, which include nonlinearities, greater depth, and stochastic training.
record.recipe_differences: The study analyzes discrete gradient dynamics in a two-layer linear network with least-squares loss and synthetic matrix reconstruction, rather than standard nonlinear networks trained on natural-label classification tasks.
record.method_sensitivity: The theoretical dynamics depend on initialization and step size; the discrete sequential-learning result assumes a sufficiently small step size and eigen-gap conditions. The experiments use a synthetic autoencoder setting.

fits_no_version.finding: Under specified initialization and step-size assumptions, two-layer linear gradient dynamics learn components sequentially and approach reduced-rank regression solutions of increasing rank. Synthetic reconstruction trajectories illustrate this behavior, unlike the single-layer dynamics.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Two-layer linear parameterization can induce sequential component learning and implicit rank regularization along the optimization path.

record.problems: The reconstruction-error values appear only in a figure and are not numerically stated. Experiments use synthetic data and a small linear model; the paper explicitly says the setting omits nonlinearities, large depth, and SGD stochasticity.
record.rows_left_out: No additional result rows omitted. Figure 2 has only the two reconstruction-error series included; its trace-norm series is not a result on the claim’s train-test generalization gap or a named version.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting alongside natural-label held-out accuracy and chance performance on random-label held-out data.
Test error as width increases beyond the width required for zero training error.
Image generalization comparisons between convolutional and fully connected networks and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive versus SGD held-out performance under limited or broader tuning.
Batch-size effects on held-out performance under fixed epoch budgets and adapted recipes.
Dropout effects on held-out error across data sizes, dropout strengths, and augmentation settings.
Magnitude-aware sharpness rankings of generalization gaps and comparisons with other measures.
Test accuracy after removing highly memorized examples versus equally many random examples.

record.verdict_notes: Table 1 evaluates covariance assumptions on classification datasets, not classification generalization. Increasing effective rank along training is not a width sweep and does not test V2. The study cites original sources but does not independently test their named findings.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label held-out accuracy coexistence.
Widening beyond interpolation and its effect on test error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image-classification generalization.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizer held-out performance.
Large-batch versus small-batch generalization under epoch budgets.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its relation to the train-test gap.
Effect of removing memorized examples on test accuracy.
